response.generated_text:
### G1-4 Incidents of corruption or bribery

Investec recognises fraud, bribery and corruption as components of financial crime and integrity risk. This risk may arise from the conduct of employees, clients, suppliers and other stakeholders and is managed through the Group’s operational risk and compliance framework.

The control framework includes an anti-bribery and corruption policy, an anti-money laundering policy, a breaches policy, and supporting compliance manuals and handbooks. These documents set out the procedures to be followed where potential corruption is identified. In accordance with regulatory requirements, employees are required to report information encountered during their employment where there are reasonable grounds for knowledge or suspicion of money laundering or terrorist-financing activity.

The Group Operational Risk and Compliance function operates a group-wide process for assessing and reporting the potential for corruption incidents. Investec’s documented approach includes business and client risk assessments; continuous monitoring of adherence to financial crime prevention policies; targeted training for specific risk roles; employee awareness campaigns; and review of external and industry developments through engagement with relevant bodies and partners. The Integrity Line provides employees with a channel to report regulatory breaches, allegations of bribery, fraud or corruption, and non-compliance with policies.

The business-conduct process was last modified on 1 June 2021. During the 2021 reporting year, 928 employees were identified as working in at-risk functions, and 100% of functions at risk were covered by anti-corruption and anti-bribery training programmes. This training coverage supports the prevention, detection and escalation of potential incidents.

### G1-4 Incidents of corruption or bribery

Investec recognises fraud, bribery and corruption as components of financial crime and integrity risk. This risk may arise from the conduct of employees, clients, suppliers and other stakeholders and is managed through the Group’s operational risk and compliance framework.

The control framework includes an anti-bribery and corruption policy, an anti-money laundering policy, a breaches policy, and supporting compliance manuals and handbooks. These documents set out the procedures to be followed where potential corruption is identified. In accordance with regulatory requirements, employees are required to report information encountered during their employment where there are reasonable grounds for knowledge or suspicion of money laundering or terrorist-financing activity.

The Group Operational Risk and Compliance function operates a group-wide process for assessing and reporting the potential for corruption incidents. Investec’s documented approach includes business and client risk assessments; continuous monitoring of adherence to financial crime prevention policies; targeted training for specific risk roles; employee awareness campaigns; and review of external and industry developments through engagement with relevant bodies and partners. The Integrity Line provides employees with a channel to report regulatory breaches, allegations of bribery, fraud or corruption, and non-compliance with policies.

The business-conduct process was last modified on 1 June 2021. During the 2021 reporting year, 928 employees were identified as working in at-risk functions, and 100% of functions at risk were covered by anti-corruption and anti-bribery training programmes. This training coverage supports the prevention, detection and escalation of potential incidents.

### G1-4 Incidents of corruption or bribery

Investec recognises fraud, bribery and corruption as components of financial crime and integrity risk. This risk may arise from the conduct of employees, clients, suppliers and other stakeholders and is managed through the Group’s operational risk and compliance framework.

The control framework includes an anti-bribery and corruption policy, an anti-money laundering policy, a breaches policy, and supporting compliance manuals and handbooks. These documents set out the procedures to be followed where potential corruption is identified. In accordance with regulatory requirements, employees are required to report information encountered during their employment where there are reasonable grounds for knowledge or suspicion of money laundering or terrorist-financing activity.

The Group Operational Risk and Compliance function operates a group-wide process for assessing and reporting the potential for corruption incidents. Investec’s documented approach includes business and client risk assessments; continuous monitoring of adherence to financial crime prevention policies; targeted training for specific risk roles; employee awareness campaigns; and review of external and industry developments through engagement with relevant bodies and partners. The Integrity Line provides employees with a channel to report regulatory breaches, allegations of bribery, fraud or corruption, and non-compliance with policies.

The business-conduct process was last modified on 1 June 2021. During the 2021 reporting year, 928 employees were identified as working in at-risk functions, and 100% of functions at risk were covered by anti-corruption and anti-bribery training programmes. This training coverage supports the prevention, detection and escalation of potential incidents.
